segments.text: It sounds crazy, but the Earth’s rotation axis is slowly shifting.
Imagine a spinning top—its wobble is similar to Earth’s motion.
This change is gravity‑induced and continuous, occurring over roughly 26,000 years.
As the axis drifts, the star that marks the celestial north pole changes.
The effect is subtle, so we don’t feel it, but over centuries the sky’s layout alters.
Understanding this drift helps astronomers track long‑term celestial changes and keep our star charts accurate.
